tests.notes: SPEC-003-001 R1/R2: reuses the CAT-07-T-006 near-duplicate video pair (dQw4w9WgXcQ / 7FwDP17XPlk), but unlike T-006 the prompt never names a URL, never says 'official', and never says 'reupload' -- it gives no tool-call target at all, only a real-world cultural description ('the classic Rickroll video'). The model must either (a) call search_youtube('Never Gonna Give You Up') to get both {video_id, title} candidates and use world knowledge to pick dQw4w9WgXcQ, or (b) recall the famous video_id directly from training data and verify it with a single decisive yt_dlp call. Either path is scoreable identically -- the scorer only checks the eventual yt_dlp call's args and the final answer's content, not which tools preceded it. Deliberately designed so the GOLD path makes exactly one call to the expected_tool (yt_dlp): scripts/score_cat07.py's _find_call() returns the FIRST call matching expected_tool by name, not the best-matching one, so a design that required two yt_dlp calls on different candidates (e.g. checking both candidates' upload_date to disambiguate) would mis-score a model that explored the wrong candidate first as bad_args even if it self-corrected -- see tests/test_score_cat07.py's paired pass/wrong-order-explored tests for both branches of this. report requires exact_match=True on the correct resource (per SPEC-003 precedent) and max_turns=5 (search hop + decisive yt_dlp hop + final answer turn, matching CAT-07-F-005's 2-hop precedent). CORRECTION (2026-08-21, from the independent Nightshift verifier's evidence gate): this max_turns=5 budget does NOT guarantee every fleet model avoids UNSCORE from turn exhaustion -- muse-glimmer-30b's live fleet run reached the correct resource by turn 2 but then looped on redundant re-verification and exhausted the budget without a final answer (UNSCORED, max_turns_exhausted_without_final_answer). A verifier probe at max_turns=10 confirmed it resolves correctly by turn 7, so the failure is a turn-budget/commitment-discipline effect, not a resource-identification failure -- see LEADERBOARD.md SS7d.

tests.notes: SPEC-003-005 R1/R2: a NEW near-duplicate video pair, deliberately chosen to be genuinely obscure -- unlike CAT-07-T-008's world-famous Rickroll pair, which every fleet model resolved via memorized world knowledge (SPEC-003-001's own finding). Both videos are real and were verified live via yt-dlp on 2026-08-21 (network access confirmed available in this worktree's sandbox -- see run report). aqz-KE-bpKQ is the real Blender Foundation YouTube channel's ('Blender', handle @BlenderOfficial) own upload of its CC-BY-licensed open movie 'Big Buck Bunny' -- yt-dlp reports the upload's license as 'Creative Commons Attribution license (reuse allowed)'. f7NwyBnIRTE is a real, unrelated channel's ('AnimalsReview') reupload of the identical film -- same 635s duration as aqz-KE-bpKQ (same underlying encode), uploaded roughly 5.5 months later. AC1 (obscurity, not just asserted): the FILM 'Big Buck Bunny' is well-known among developers as a CC test video (comparable to 'Never Gonna Give You Up' being a well-known song for T-008), but neither specific video ID here is documented/memorized training data anywhere near the density of dQw4w9WgXcQ, which recurs in essentially every internet rickroll reference -- there is no equivalent single canonical-ID fact pattern for Big Buck Bunny's many reuploads, so a model must actually retrieve and read tool output (title text) to tell the two apart, rather than recall an ID. AC5 (query-specificity/threshold-pruning, the SPEC-003-004 finding this spec's Problem addendum required addressing) -- CORRECTED (2026-08-21) after the live fleet run below: the two titles ('Big Buck Bunny 60fps 4K - Official Blender Foundation Short Film' vs 'Animated Short Film "Big Buck Bunny", 4K, Full Length') share a token core (big/buck/bunny/short/film/4k), so a query built from those shared, generic descriptor words (e.g. 'Big Buck Bunny', 'Big Buck Bunny short film 4k', 'Big Buck Bunny official studio') surfaces BOTH candidates under search_youtube's 0.6 query-token-recall threshold -- verified both by a standalone probe (cat07_harness.execute_search_youtube) and empirically, live, in 2 of 5 fleet transcripts (qwen/qwen3.6-27b: query 'Big Buck Bunny'; gemma-4-31b-it: query 'Big Buck Bunny official studio'), both of which then read the two returned titles and correctly picked aqz-KE-bpKQ by its 'Official Blender Foundation' text -- genuine search-and-compare disambiguation (AC2 evidence, not pure recall). HOWEVER a query that leans on the DISAMBIGUATING words themselves ('Blender', 'Foundation', 'official') without also repeating a shared descriptor word DOES prune to the single correct candidate (e.g. 'Big Buck Bunny Blender Foundation official' -> only aqz-KE-bpKQ, 6/6 query tokens but only 3/6 overlap with the OTHER title's tokens, just under 0.6) -- observed live in 2 of 5 fleet transcripts (ornith-1.0-35b's first search; muse-glimmer-30b's 2nd/3rd searches, after it had already seen both candidates and yt_dlp'd both). This is a real instance of the Problem addendum's accepted branch ("accept as realistic tool behavior -- a real search index would do the same"): a more specific query narrowing to the one correct result is not case-design failure, and in the live run it never determined a model's outcome by itself (ornith and muse-glimmer's failures were unrelated turn-budget/looping issues after they had already resolved the correct video_id -- see run report). The original written claim here (a design guarantee that pruning was "structurally unlikely regardless of phrasing") did not survive contact with live model queries and has been corrected to the evidence above rather than left standing -- see tests/test_score_cat07.py for both the both-candidates-surfaced and prunes-to-one-candidate regressions, pinned to the real queries observed. Deliberately, as with T-008, the gold path makes exactly ONE decisive yt_dlp call (on aqz-KE-bpKQ): scripts/score_cat07.py's _find_call() first-match semantics mean a model that probes f7NwyBnIRTE first and only later self-corrects would still score bad_args on that first call -- see tests/test_score_cat07.py's paired pass/wrong-order-explored tests for both branches of this, mirroring CAT-07-T-008's precedent exactly. max_turns=5 matches CAT-07-T-008's precedent (search hop + decisive yt_dlp hop + final answer turn, with slack for one extra exploratory call).

Two NEW corpus files added by this case: test_data/cat07/transcripts/aqz-KE-bpKQ.json and test_data/cat07/transcripts/f7NwyBnIRTE.json, each carrying its own source_note per NFR-001 V1.
